ratings.note: Any report carrying one of these routine keyboard, dialog, live-region or state findings fails the skill's own lint, so the agent must hand-edit tool-generated text on most audits and learns to distrust the gate.

Every rater and verifier packet that cites evidence is affected, fresh subagents cannot know the base, and the likely fallback of judging from text alone weakens independent rating and verification without any sign in the report.
Each fresh subagent wastes a few reads hunting for the schema, and one that gives up may write output that does not validate, but a single file search avoids it.

Losing form data on Back is a classic high-impact defect that the probes cannot exercise, so the agent must script it outside the skill, leaving the evidence outside the run record, or leave it untested.
Every heuristic packet built with journeys leaks the correct path and the avoided labels, which silently breaks evaluator independence and inflates detection counts and benchmark recall.
Any multi-role audit produces these near-duplicates that the merge never proposes, and the repeats inflate the finding count and push problems listed once down the priority order.
It only happens when a second rating batch is built, but then ratings are silently attached to the wrong findings, corrupting the severities that set report and fix priority.
An unexplained empty queue sends the agent on a diagnosis detour and invites a false 'nothing to fix', though an agent that knows to merge and promote first avoids it.
On the occasional split request the lead must hand-edit candidate JSON, re-merge and re-verify, which is slow and puts provenance at risk.
